extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, peer reviewers, and researchers studying peer review
extracted.subtask_description: A synthesized taxonomy of criteria for evaluating manuscripts and review reports in scientific peer review, plus identified bias risks and procedural recommendations for editors and reviewers. Intended to guide review quality assessment, reviewer training, and editorial policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance / significance of the research problem
rubrics_metrics.description: Importance / significance of the research problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the topic addresses an important problem or question for the field; linked to selection and allocation functions of peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Originality / novelty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether the work offers new ideas, findings, approaches, or perspectives relative to existing literature; guards against redundancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theoretical sophistication / conceptual clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Theoretical sophistication / conceptual clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the soundness and clarity of the theoretical framework or conceptual argumentation; includes conceptual rigor and coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soundness of methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Soundness of methodology — design, controls, statistical treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine study design, experimental controls, statistical analyses, and whether methods are appropriate to answer the research question; relates to reproducibility and validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity of conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Validity of conclusions — do the data support the claims?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether interpretations and claims are supported by the presented data and analyses; check for overclaiming or unwarranted inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility / verifiability of the procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Reproducibility / verifiability of the procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether methods and reporting are sufficiently detailed to permit replication or verification; includes data and code availability where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy of literature integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Adequacy of literature integration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the manuscript appropriately situates itself within prior work, cites relevant studies, and critically engages the literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of writing and presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of writing and presentation (clarity, structure, length).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider clarity, organization, readability, and adherence to length/formatting norms; poor presentation can obscure substantive merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethical conduct — IRB approval, conflict of interest, attribution, fabrication signals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for appropriate ethical approvals, disclosure of conflicts, correct attribution, and any signs of data fabrication or misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical applicability / generalisability
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical applicability / generalisability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the extent to which findings generalize beyond study conditions and whether there are clear practical or theoretical implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage (of review report)
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage — does the review address each substantive dimension of the manuscript?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A high-quality review should systematically comment on the manuscript's main substantive dimensions (e.g., importance, methods, conclusions) rather than only on peripheral issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity (of review comments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specificity — are comments tied to specific passages with line/page references?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review comments should point to particular passages, figures, or sections (line/page references) so authors can locate and address concerns; avoids vague criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantiation (of reviewers' claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantiation — are claims backed by argument, citation, or example?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review assertions should be supported by reasoning, examples, or references; unsubstantiated assertions reduce review usefulness and credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructiveness (actionable feedback)
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructiveness — does the review give the author an actionable path forward?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good reviews provide specific suggestions for improvement and prioritize issues so authors can revise effectively; distinguishes developmental from purely evaluative comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone / civility
rubrics_metrics.description: Tone / civility — is the review free of ad hominem and rhetorical hostility?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews should be respectful and professional; hostile or abusive language undermines constructive discourse and can bias editorial decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal consistency (between narrative and recommendation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal consistency — do the narrative comments cohere with the numeric recommendation?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that the written critique aligns with the overall recommendation (e.g., 'accept' vs. negative narrative). Discrepancies should be explained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness (of review delivery)
rubrics_metrics.description: Timeliness — was the review delivered in time?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt reviews support efficient editorial workflows; tardy reviews can delay decisions and harms authors. Journals may factor timeliness into reviewer selection or incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriateness of recommendation — does the recommendation track the substantive critique?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the acceptance/rejection/revision recommendation follows from the substantive strengths and weaknesses identified in the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three functions of peer review: Selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection — gatekeeping the literature (allocation of journal space).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When peer review is used primarily for selection, emphasis should be on criteria like importance, originality, theoretical contribution, methodological soundness, and validity of conclusions (items A1–A5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Three functions of peer review: Improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Improvement — developmental shaping of accepted manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When peer review aims to improve manuscripts, emphasis shifts to review report qualities such as coverage, specificity, substantiation, constructiveness, and tone (items B11–B15).

rubrics_metrics.name: Three functions of peer review: Allocation of recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Allocation of recognition — symbolic certification of work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When peer review serves to allocate recognition, emphasis is on markers of merit such as importance and practical applicability/generalizability (items A1 and A10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirmation / theoretical bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirmation / theoretical bias (reviewers favor work that confirms their own theoretical preferences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should self-check for favoring work that aligns with their theoretical commitments; awareness and procedures (e.g., blinding) can mitigate this bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliation / institutional prestige bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Affiliation / institutional prestige bias (evaluative bias favoring authors from prestigious institutions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors and reviewers should be aware that perceived institutional prestige can unduly influence judgments; procedures like double-blind review may reduce this effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Gender bias (systematic differences in assessment by author gender).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize and mitigate gender-based disparities in review outcomes through training, monitoring, and potentially masking author identities where feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nationality / language bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Nationality / language bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be attentive to biases against authors based on nationality or non-native language use; focus critique on scientific content rather than perceived language shortcomings and provide constructive guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cronyism (favoring known authors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cronyism (favouring known authors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid preferential treatment for acquaintances or collaborators; disclose conflicts of interest and recuse when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conservatism bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Conservatism bias — bias against high-risk / heterodox work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should be aware they may unduly favor safe, conventional research; editorial policies can encourage fair assessment of novel or high-risk submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirmation of priority / Matthew effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirmation of priority by senior authors (Matthew effect).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beware tendencies to reward established authors disproportionately; measures to anonymize authorship or balance reviewer pools can help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of structured review forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of structured review forms mapping to dimensions A1–A10.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structured forms that explicitly list manuscript-quality dimensions (importance, originality, methods, etc.) help standardize assessments and enable per-dimension scoring and aggregation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent multiple review (3+)
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent multiple review (3+) with explicit per-dimension scoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtaining multiple independent reviews and scoring each dimension facilitates more reliable editorial decisions and reduces single-reviewer idiosyncrasies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor adjudication of substantive disagreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Editor adjudication of substantive disagreement before decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should resolve conflicting substantive assessments (rather than relying solely on counts of recommendations), possibly soliciting additional reviews or consulting senior editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and feedback to reviewers on RQI-style metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Training and feedback to reviewers on RQI-style metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing reviewers with training and feedback (e.g., on Review Quality Instrument metrics) can improve review quality and consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-blind or open review to mitigate biases
rubrics_metrics.description: Where possible, double-blind or open review to mitigate identified biases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt blinding (to reduce affiliation/nationality/gender bias) or open review (to increase transparency and accountability) depending on journal goals and context.
